The surface trough extending from Tropical Storm Saudel is slowly 
moving out of the Marianas with some scattered locally heavy showers 
and isolated thunderstorms remaining. Showers and isolated 
thunderstorms are expected to become isolated tomorrow for Guam with 
coverage remaining low-end scattered for Tinian and Saipan. A col 
looks to develop over the region Friday ahead of current Tropical 
Storm Saudel, which will likely allow for potential island-effect 
showers and isolated thunderstorms, particularly over Guam. By 
Friday night or Saturday, winds will begin picking back up as Saudel 
approaches. Current model guidance continues to indicate a passage 
through the far northern Marianas, placing Guam and the CNMI within 
its monsoonal tail. Thus, elevated winds, increasing showers, and 
thunderstorms are a possibility from the weekend through midweek. 
Residents of the Marianas should continue to monitor the forecast.

Marine...
Gentle to moderate winds today will be slowly easing over the next
few days. Higher winds are still possible with thunderstorms tonight.
Combined seas of 4 to 5 feet will persist through the week and begin
building ahead of Tropical Storm Saudel. A wetter weekend with 
elevated winds, locally heavy showers, and potentially hazardous seas
may be in store depending on the development of Saudel, 
particularly for Tinian and Saipan. This situation will continue to 
be monitored closely.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Depression 17W was just upgraded to Tropical Storm Saudel. 
Saudel is centered near 8.9 degrees north and 153.9 degrees east. 
Maximum sustained winds are 40 mph, and Saudel is expected to 
continue to intensify, and could even start to intensify rapidly on 
Friday. Saudel has been moving north at 5 mph, and is expected to 
turn toward the northwest with an increase in forward speed.

Numerous showers and scattered thunderstorms are found between 6N and
9N from 151E to 154E. Farther out, also associated with the monsoon
trough, scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms are found in a
curved band that stretches from Wake Island to the Marianas to Yap to
Chuuk to east of Majuro.

For further information on Tropical Storm Saudel, please refer to the
Local Statement issued by the National Weather Service under WMO
header WTPQ81 PGUM, the Tropical Cyclone Public Advisory issued by
the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM, the
Tropical Cyclone Warning issued by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center
under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW, and the Significant Tropical Weather
Advisory under WMO head ABPW10 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
The monsoon trough is currently dominating the weather in Eastern
Micronesia. This is a bit unusual and is related to the fact that
we're currently in a Strong El Nino pattern. Strong monsoon activity
will likely continue for at least a couple more months. When it
decays, as the El Nino peaks and starts decaying, it will likely do 
so with a vengeance. Most of Micronesia is typically plunged into a 
drought of epic proportions. So enjoy the rain while you are able, 
and collect as much as you can. The times of plenty could fade fast 
enough, potentially leaving you with nothing.

Western Micronesia...
Tropical Depression 17W was upgraded to Tropical Storm Saudel by the
Joint Typhoon Warning Center and continues to consolidate as it 
moves north-northwest and away from Chuuk State. Strong westerly 
winds are ongoing south of the circulation and will continue to 
impact Chuuk, with 40 kt gusts possible Thursday. Heavy showers, 
flash flooding, mudslides, and gusty winds will continue to impact 
Chuuk over the next few days. A Small Craft Advisory is in effect 
until Friday afternoon for Chuuk. 

Additional rainfall amounts of 3 to 5 inches are possible through 
the week. These rainfall amounts could continue to pose flash 
flooding and potential mudslide risk. In the latter half of the 
week, a monsoon surge will develop and continue to impact Chuuk with 
gusty winds and seas hazardous to small craft. Residents across Chuuk
State should monitor local forecasts and heed advice of emergency 
managers when heavy rainfall occurs.

Elsewhere in western Micronesia, showers and thunderstorms are
expected to increase significantly at Palau and Yap over the coming
days. This is caused by an intensifying monsoon surge along the
southern peripheries of a developing trough axis stretching from the
aforementioned TS Saudel westward, which will change orientation as
Saudel approaches the Far Northern Marianas. Intense showers and
thunderstorms are expected to peak at Yap tonight and Thursday, to
then taper down slowly thereafter. Meanwhile at Palau, a secondary
convergence zone will develop to bring peak shower and thunder
